question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}3x, & \,y<x<1\,,\,0<y<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Find $P(\frac{1}{4}<X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{6}).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(X\in A\,|\,Y=y)={\int }_{A}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}y,
$$

where ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$  

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{y}^{1}3x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{y}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(1-{y}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}(1-{y}^{2}), & \,0<y<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)}.
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $y<x<1\,,\,0<y<1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{3x}{(\frac{3}{2}(1-{y}^{2}))} \\  & =\frac{2x}{1-{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2x}{1-{y}^{2}}, & \,0<y<x<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute our probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{4}<X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{6}) & =P(\frac{1}{4}<X\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{6}) \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y=\frac{1}{6})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1}\frac{2x}{(1-{(\frac{1}{6})}^{2})}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1}\frac{2x}{(\frac{35}{36})}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{36}{35}{\int }_{1/4}^{1}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{36}{35}{[{x}^{2}]}_{1/4}^{1} \\  & =\frac{36}{35}(1-\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{27}{28}.\end{aligned}
$$
